messages:
Sofia Rivera: Noticed a few production traces where a service account exchange returned a token for a different project than the incoming request. Example trace id: tr-6f1c.
Arjun Patel: Do we have the gateway trace? Which route was called?
Sofia Rivera: /v1/completions via api-gw-east, caller=svc:image-ingest, caller_project=org-alpha/proj-42, issued_project=org-alpha/proj-99. Request succeeded.
Nora Chen: If the router falls back to a compatible SA, that could explain it. We have a "compatible fallback" rule to avoid hard failures when a specific token is exhausted.
Arjun Patel: Yikes. That fallback was supposed to preserve billing attribution, not change it. Is billing being charged to issued_project?
Sofia Rivera: Yes — billing shows charge on proj-99. Customer noticed unexpected cost.
Nora Chen: Short-term mitigation: add an auth-proxy assertion flag `exchange_mismatch=true` to logs and to our auth_events stream. Also add a quota/charge attribution override so cost goes to caller_project unless explicit consent.
DevOps Bot: Note: Deploy scheduled - auth-proxy patch (canary) at 2025-07-08T18:00Z by Arjun Patel.
Arjun Patel: Proposed policy change: disallow silent compatible fallbacks by default. Require callers to opt in with a header `X-Confirm-Project-Swap: yes` or via console opt-in at org-admin level.
Sofia Rivera: UX ask: when console generates an exchange that would assign a different project, show a one-line warning: "This exchange will issue tokens for Project X instead of Project Y. Continue?" with a checkbox to persist consent.
Nora Chen: Telemetry: SQL to find mismatches:
```
SELECT event_time, caller_project, issued_project, trace_id
FROM auth_events
WHERE event_type='token_exchange' AND issued_project != caller_project
ORDER BY event_time DESC
LIMIT 200;
```
Arjun Patel: Rollout plan: 1) add telemetry and alert (>=5 mismatches/min triggers pager), 2) canary block of compatible fallback (return 403 instead), 3) add header opt-in path, 4) console opt-in + consent UI.
Sofia Rivera: Also add a billing rule: if fallback occurs without explicit consent, bill to caller_project and emit a billing-discrepancy event for manual review.
Nora Chen: SRE runbook: if alert fires, immediately flip fallback to blocked, search for recent traces with `exchange_mismatch=true`, and contact affected teams.
Arjun Patel: Docs update: examples for safe exchange and migration guide for clients that relied on fallback behavior. Include snippet:
```
# client side
headers = {
  'Authorization': 'Bearer ...',
  'X-Confirm-Project-Swap': 'yes'
}
```
Sofia Rivera: I'll open an RFC and attach the SQL, header spec, console mock, and rollout checklist. Link WIP once ready.
DevOps Bot: RFC created: rfc/avoid-silent-project-fallback (draft) by Sofia Rivera.
Arjun Patel: Thanks. I'll own the canary deploy and metric dashboard for the next 48h.
Nora Chen: Adding @billing and @console-ux to review the consent language.
Sofia Rivera: Filing a follow-up ticket to reconcile any historical misattributed charges.
Arjun Patel: Great—let's prioritize the telemetry first so we can measure scope before blocking.
